newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes track WTI rally late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes track WTI rally late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices followed a late rally in West Texas Intermediate (WTI) as refiners scrambled for supplies ahead of the deadline for pipeline nominations.
With October flows starting the 1st, California traders needed to ensure they were adequately supplied. Potential existed for last-minute deals to meet shipping obligations.
Meanwhile, cash November WTI ended 15-20 cents above Tuesday, with Alaska North Slope (ANS) differentials unchanged at $2.30 under.
ANS outright prices were $21.90/22.20 a barrel.
With differentials unchanged from the last October deal and a 30-cent roll against November, buyers said the market was indicated at minus $2.60.
Line 63 remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for October delivery.
California heavy crude Kern River was unchanged despite prospects for last minute deals ahead of pipeline scheduling. Levels held at $16.15/16.35 a barrel.
And prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.60/17.70.
